identity.title: The evolving jet spectrum of the neutron star X-ray binary Aql X-1 in transitional states during its 2016 outburst

paper_type_evidence.quote: We observed Aql X–1 during August and September 2016 at radio, mm, IR, optical and X-ray wavelengths with the Australia Telescope Compact Array (ATCA), ALMA, the VLT

evidence.quote: Its distance was determined from type I X-ray bursts to be 4.5–6 kpc
The peak of radio emission is centred on average at (J2000) 19:11:16.024 $\pm$ 0.005 +00:35:05.900 $\pm$ 0.007

question.value: How does the optically thick-to-thin jet spectral break of the neutron star LMXB Aql X-1 evolve across state transitions in its 2016 outburst, and does it move to lower frequencies in softer states as in BH XRBs?

evidence.quote: The goal was to study the behaviour of the jet break over the transitional states for the first time in a NS LMXB and to test the hypothesis that the jet break moves to lower frequencies
This paper makes use of the following ALMA data: ADS/JAO.ALMA#2015.1.00734.T.
for the three observations in band 3 and at 295.99, 297.93, 307.99 and 309.99 GHz for the observations in band 7

frequencies_and_spectral_setup.value: four spectral windows of 2 GHz each; 31.2 MHz resolution; band 3 centred 90.49, 92.43, 102.49, 104.49 GHz; band 7 centred 295.99, 297.93, 307.99, 309.99 GHz

evidence.quote: All observations were set up to use four spectral windows, each with a bandwidth of 2 GHz.
The spectral resolution for each spectral window was 31.2 MHz.
The observations were performed using between 38 and 46 12-m antennas.
The maximum baseline length was 1.4 and 3.1 km, for the August and September observations, respectively.
At 97.49 GHz (band 3), the synthesised beam size was between 0.46$^{\prime\prime}$$\times$0.35$^{\prime\prime}$and 0.71$^{\prime\prime}$$\times$0.50$^{\prime\prime}$, depending on the epoch.
All observations were taken simultaneously in two 2-GHz frequency bands, centred at 5.5 and 9.0 GHz.

provided.value: X-ray spectra and light curves for state classification

evidence.quote: $\it Swift$/XRT observed Aql X–1 at numerous times during its 2016 outburst

provided.value: mid-IR, near-IR and optical photometry for SEDs

evidence.quote: Mid-IR observations of the field of Aql X–1 were made with the VLT on the 3rd and 4th of August 2016

what.value: Suzaku spectra of 2011 outburst (periods P0, P9) for state comparison

evidence.quote: we extracted the spectra from the $\it Suzaku$ X-ray Imaging Spectrometer (cite: Koyama2007) and the Hard X-ray Detector (cite: Takahashi2007) instruments corresponding to periods P0 and P9

what.value: Hydrogen column density N_H = 4.4e21 cm-2 used for extinction

evidence.quote: We re-calibrated the datasets for these observations flagging out the problematic antennas before re-generating the images.
We re-generated images from the ALMA calibrated products following standard procedures with CASA v4.7.

analysis_steps.goal: Re-image ALMA data and measure flux densities

method.value: Re-calibrated band 7 with problem antennas flagged, imaged with CASA, fitted elliptical Gaussian in image plane; error is image rms

evidence.quote: The reported flux density for all sources in this section corresponds to the peak flux from the elliptical Gaussian fitted to the source emission in the image plane
extracted with Briggs weighting and robust=0.5 for all the observations

validation.value: Re-calibrated images show point-like emission, flux densities increased by >~50%

evidence.quote: These images show point-like source emission, similarly to the band 3 observations.

method.value: Subtract confusing source and field sources in uv-plane, fit target in uv-plane with uvmultifit

evidence.quote: we adopted the values obtained with the second method (the $uv$-plane fitting)

validation.value: Confusing source flux at 9 GHz consistent with VLA expectation; image-plane and uv-plane values broadly consistent

evidence.quote: fully consistent with the 134 $\mu$Jy expected at 9 GHz from the measured VLA spectrum

analysis_steps.goal: Classify accretion state from X-ray spectra

method.value: Fit Swift/XRT (and NuSTAR) spectra with tbabs*nthcomp(+diskbb, rfxconv), constrained by comparison with Suzaku spectra of previous outbursts

evidence.quote: we used a basic model consisting of thermal Comptonisation absorbed from neutral material (`tbabs*nthcomp` in XSPEC) and, where necessary, we added a disc blackbody

key_parameters.value: min 20 counts per bin; XRT 0.4–9 keV, NuSTAR 3–30 keV

evidence.quote: used the 0.4–9 keV energy range for analysis

assumptions.value: 1.4 Msun neutron star, distance 5.2 kpc for Eddington fractions

evidence.quote: the Eddington fraction during obs 2a/2b is $\sim$60–65% for a 1.4 M$_{\odot}$ neutron star

fitting.value: chi-square fitting with simultaneous fits and tied parameters

evidence.loc: Observations and data analysis, Swift and NuSTAR
evidence.quote: we can attempt to constrain the two-component models by fitting all the spectra simultaneously and linking the column density of the absorbing material, expected to be constant.
Our obs 1 perfectly matches the P0 interval

analysis_steps.goal: Fit radio-to-mm spectral slopes and break frequencies

method.value: Power-law slopes F_nu ∝ nu^alpha before/after the break (first four/last three points for obs 1 and 3); upper limit on break from extrapolating thick spectrum to 200 and 250 GHz

evidence.quote: we used the first four points/last three points to determine the spectral slope before/after the break

analysis_steps.goal: Test correlation of break frequency with X-ray hardness/flux

method.value: Spearman rank test of break frequency vs hardness ratio and MAXI/ASM count rate

evidence.loc: 4.2 Evolution of the jet spectral break along the outburst
evidence.quote: While a Spearman rank test yields a positive correlation of 90$\%$ between the jet break frequency and the hardness of the X-ray spectrum

validation.value: chance probability >5% given 2 degrees of freedom

evidence.loc: Discussion, Evolution of the jet spectral break along the outburst
evidence.quote: such a correlation still has a chance probability $>$ 5$\%$ given the low number of degrees of freedom (2).

findings_qualitative.value: Radio and mm emission with negative spectral slope detected in the soft state at 60–65% Eddington, unlike earlier outbursts where radio was quenched

evidence.quote: Our observations 2a and 2b demonstrate the existence of radio to mm emission with a negative slope after the source has transited into the soft state

claims.hypothesis: The jet break moves to lower frequencies as the NS evolves to softer states, as in BH MAXI J1836-194
claims.experiment: Quasi-simultaneous ATCA, ALMA and IR/X-ray SEDs at four epochs
claims.result: Break ~100 GHz in hard/intermediate obs 1 and 3; below ~5 GHz in soft obs 2a/2b
claims.finding: Break frequency evolves with state in a NS as in BHs

evidence.quote: evolve from having a spectral break from optically thick to thin emission at $\sim$100 GHz during hard/intermediate states to below $\sim$5 GHz during soft states

claims.hypothesis: Break frequency correlates with X-ray hardness

evidence.loc: 4.2 Evolution of the jet spectral break along the outburst
evidence.quote: Thus, more data are needed to confirm this correlation in Aql X–1.

limitations_admitted.value: Observations not strictly simultaneous, spanning many hours across transitions; X-ray spectral model degeneracy

evidence.quote: Besides the spectral degeneracy, a caveat to the classification above is that the multi-wavelength observations span several hours.

referee_caveats_inferred: Only four epochs, so the correlation tests have ~2 degrees of freedom
Break frequency in obs 1 and 3 poorly constrained, sparse points
X-ray models for obs 2a and 3 were imposed rather than fitted
